summary: This paper advances the theory of flexible list coloring of d-degenerate graphs by establishing four major results: a sharpened discrete min-cut recurrence and Padé shift theorem lowering the sub-2d crossover threshold; a generalized s-rank global palette-order theorem breaking the Theta(1/d^3) barrier to Omega(1/d^2) for bounded conflict requests; a universal (2d+3)-vertex d-degenerate mutual-exclusion family ruling out universal (d+1, epsilon)-flexibility for epsilon > 1/4; and the exact d=1 forest double-optimum alongside the asymptotic flow-framework barrier (2-1/e)d. All results are fully verified in Lean 4 and exact-Q Python scripts.
strengths: Complete formal verification in Lean 4.36.0 with zero sorry, zero grind, and zero custom axioms.
Sharp combinatorial improvements lowering sub-2d crossover thresholds and breaking Theta(1/d^3) via s-rank palette ordering.
Comprehensive computational and cryptographic validation with 16 SHA-256 certificates and 73 passing adversarial tests.
weaknesses: Some proofs rely on dense technical calculations involving discrete recurrences that require the accompanying Lean mechanization for absolute security.
The gap between epsilon = 1/4 and 1/(d+1) for d >= 3 remains open.
strong_novelty_candidates: Sharpened Discrete Min-Cut Recurrence and Padé Shift eliminating double-counting via exact indicator identity.
Generalized s-Rank Global Palette-Order Theorem achieving Omega(1/d^2) for bounded-conflict request assignments.
Universal All-d Mutual-Exclusion Family Gd on 2d + 3 vertices generalizing d=2 gadgets to all degeneracies.
